sections.title: CS and AI developments
sections.content:
Multimodal pretraining

A new study finds that shared attention and normalization with modality-specific feed-forward layers can provide a common routing space without forcing every modality through identical capacity. Early joint training outperformed late alignment; the preferred design was scaled to a 13.5B MoE trained on two trillion tokens. The result is a fresh preprint, so the claimed generality still depends on replication across other data mixtures. Paper

Spatial Evidence Graphs

A training-free verifier maps intermediate visual-spatial claims to entities, relations, source steps and geometric evidence, then repairs reasoning from the earliest contradicted claim. It reports 68.94% average accuracy across 15 settings, 8.55 points over compared baselines. Its bottleneck may move to object localization and geometry rather than disappear. Paper

sections.title: Technical idea: delta-state CRDTs send joinable changes
sections.content: State-based CRDTs tolerate unreliable, duplicated delivery by joining whole states; operation-based CRDTs send small messages but need stronger dissemination guarantees. A delta-state CRDT returns a small joinable state fragment for each mutation. Idempotent, commutative and associative joins make retransmission, reordering and batching safe. Anti-entropy still has to retain delta intervals until peers acknowledge them and sometimes fall back to a larger state transfer. The general pattern is a joinable partial snapshot that preserves full-snapshot recovery semantics. Paper

sections.title: Non-CS science: a maternal vaccine route against infant GBS
sections.content: GBS can pass from a colonized pregnant person to a newborn and cause sepsis, pneumonia or meningitis. In a phase 1/2 study of the six-valent maternal vaccine GBS6, 216 pregnant participants received vaccine or placebo and 209 infants were born. Adverse-event frequencies were similar, and vaccine-induced antibodies crossed the placenta into infants. This was a safety and immunogenicity trial, not proof that disease incidence falls; a larger efficacy trial is still required. A successful vaccine could reduce reliance on labour-time antibiotics and potentially protect against late-onset disease. Trial

sections.title: Geopolitics and political economy
sections.content:
• Taiwan: Han Kuang drills moved President Lai and senior officials by armoured carrier to a command centre and include degraded mobile internet, testing continuity of government rather than only combat units. Reuters
  • ICC: Washington is using bilateral leverage to encourage withdrawals after Venezuela and Chad announced exits, weakening universality without formally abolishing the court. Le Monde
  • Gaza: the roadmap remains a sequencing problem: Hamas demands withdrawal and aid first; Israel demands disarmament first. Without verifiable ordering and penalties, an endpoint list is not an implementation plan. Reuters
  • Eurozone: July composite PMI reached 52.0 and services 51.7, but France remained in contraction, limiting how far area-wide resilience translates into French fiscal room. Reuters

sections.title: Marxist fragment
sections.content:
“Finance capital strives for domination, not freedom.”

Lenin uses Hilferding’s formulation against treating imperialism as a detachable policy. Concentrated, mobile capital seeks protected markets, debtor discipline, strategic infrastructure and political conditions securing returns. This need not mean open dictatorship: formally liberal law can coexist with coercive constraints on states, workers and debtor populations. Primary text

sections.title: Two philosophy and political fragments
sections.content:
John Stuart Mill

“He who knows only his own side of the case, knows little of that.”

For Mill, serious understanding requires meeting an opposing view in the form its committed defenders consider strongest. That is epistemic humility and also causal discipline: denunciation is not an explanation of why rival institutions reproduce consent. Primary text

Benjamin Constant

“By creating credit, it places authority itself in a position of dependence.”

Credit can restrain arbitrary rulers by raising the cost of confiscation, default and chaos, but the restraint is not neutral: government becomes dependent on holders of mobile wealth, whose veto can obstruct despotism and redistribution alike. Primary text

sections.title: French usage: ça me dépasse
sections.content: Ça me dépasse means “I can’t understand that,” “that is beyond me,” or morally “I can’t believe people would do that.” It is stronger than je ne comprends pas. Example: Comment ce bug peut disparaître quand on ajoute un print ? Ça me dépasse. Je suis dépassé instead means overwhelmed or unable to keep up; ça dépasse mes compétences means outside one’s expertise. CNRTL

sections.title: Music corner
sections.content: Three direct recommendations. Open the combined YouTube queue.

items.label: Classical
items.piece: J. S. Bach — Chromatic Fantasia and Fugue in D minor, BWV 903
items.description: A 12-minute solo-piano work that uses the short-form slot without becoming a miniature. The fantasia moves through rapid scales, broken chords and recitative-like pauses with an almost improvisatory volatility; the fugue then converts that instability into a strict, accumulating argument. It should fit your preference for strong forward motion and structural payoff while testing a more chromatic and rhetorically free Bach than the concertos you already know.

items.label: Jazz / fusion
items.description: A compact modern-fusion track built around an immediately legible keyboard motif, displaced accents and tightly coordinated ensemble turns. The rhythmic complexity remains attached to a recurring tune rather than becoming an end in itself, which makes it a better fit than recent pieces that registered as technically active but diffuse or merely atmospheric.

items.label: Other
items.description: French psychedelic pop with a concise melodic hook, dry surf-guitar colour, organ and a brisk arrangement that keeps introducing small changes instead of stretching one loop. It is adjacent to the successful French groove lane of Cortex and L’Impératrice, but shifts the test toward songcraft, garage-pop texture and deadpan vocal delivery rather than disco or jazz-funk.

sections.title: Unrelated fact: Marshallese charts modelled waves, not coastlines
sections.content: Marshallese stick charts encoded swell reflection, refraction and interference around islands. Cowrie shells could mark atolls, while mattang worked as training models for wave–island interactions. They were generally studied on land rather than carried at sea: navigators memorized the model, then read swell direction and disturbed water through sight and the felt motion of the canoe. Smithsonian Ocean

sections.title: Puzzle: Molyneux’s newly sighted geometer
sections.content: A person born blind learns to distinguish a cube from a sphere by touch, then gains sight. Before touching them again, can they identify the visible cube and sphere? A yes answer assumes sufficiently amodal spatial representation; a no answer requires learned mapping between tactile and visual spaces. State the representation or learning mechanism your answer assumes and what observation would change your mind. Background
